question: Which 18th-century revolt was led by Raja Chait Singh against British interference in the Benares region in 1781?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Benares Revolt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The revolt occurred due to the imposition of excessive demands and interference by the British in the affairs of the **Benares region.**
 
• **Raja Chait Singh **was arrested by the British, but he managed to escape, leading to widespread rebellion among his followers in the region.
 
• The **Benares Revolt** is considered one of the early instances of resistance against British colonial policies in India.
 
• **Raja Chait Singh **was the ruler of Benares and ascended the throne in the **1770s**. He was a vassal of the British East India Company but resented British interference in his administration.
 
• The British administration under **Warren Hastings** imposed heavy tax demands on Indian rulers to finance their wars and administration.
 
• Though the revolt was suppressed, it signaled the growing unrest among Indian rulers against British policies.
 
• The **Chuar Revolt**: Occurred in **West Bengal** during the late 18th century. It was a tribal rebellion against British exploitation.
 
• The **Santhal Revolt**: Took place in **1855**, led by the Santhal community against exploitation by landlords and the British.

 
• **Significance of Early Revolts:**

 
 
• They also highlighted the socio-political changes brought about by colonial interference in traditional systems.
